assessments.reasoning: Wayback capture 20060427110041id_ preserves OSI’s www.opensource.org:80/licenses/afl-2.0.php. The 17,725-byte witness reports the claim’s revision digest. OSI’s title and heading identify v2.0, the application notice repeats the version, and sections 1–3 grant copyright, patent and source-code rights. The page credits Lawrence E. Rosen and says the author ceased to use or recommend the license.

The Index’s pinned SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 expressly includes historical editions. Its admission table at bytes [533,942) applies to the identifiable v2.0 grant published by OSI. AFL family membership alone would be insufficient to identify the edition.

OSI’s license-discuss archive identifies Lawrence Rosen as sender of message 021969 on 8 September 2021, SHA-256 203753e50d9da13cd4e735867cbc305b07b25e251d62f17c4d84f7702636e245. His quoted earlier message at bytes [5751,5874) addresses AFL and OSL before 3.0. His reply recalls board approval and endorses 3.0. Brasseur reports uncertainty about documentary proof. These statements support the limited historical context. Smith proposed the word “superseded.”

The Index decision at afb962e68831a16accb80c70159b1e2f1fbb4dbc, bytes [1237,1431), names permanent ID b1ac3019c7f046ff9475fb9f735e867a, Academic Free License v2.0, afl-2-0, sha256:59e40a43b6eecc300bb2327db5a3af932a4ab5a9a961e2aeef1fcd0ae71a80fc, license, historical. The opaque ID and revision match the claim. AFL v3.0 has a distinct ID, digest and active value.

challenge.method: Compared the article with the AFL 3.0 sidebar link, the AFL 2.1 website footer and the neighboring AFL rows. Checked who used the terms “no longer valid” and “superseded,” and whether either statement established retroactive termination.
challenge.results: The body and required work notice both identify v2.0. The sidebar and footer refer to different editions. Rosen asked for removal of pre-3.0 forms, while McCoy Smith proposed retaining them as superseded for legacy uses. The exchange records that difference. It supplies no determination terminating a particular grant. The Index independently chose historical.

limitations: The Internet Archive preserves the OSI publication. Rosen’s mailing-list reply is a participant’s recollection of approval. The supplied evidence includes no edition-specific board decision or SPDX deprecation decision.

Historical denotes retention for reconciliation. The legal effect on existing grants, application to a particular work, reuse of the captured HTML, installation eligibility and consumer release authorization remain separate.
reasoning: The archived OSI publication identifies Academic Free License v2.0 in its heading, application notice and operative grants. The Index admits earlier editions and assigns historical to this exact reference. The 2021 correspondence supplies evidence of the author’s treatment of pre-3.0 editions.
